title: France War Trails — Iepe & Sietze
subtitle: A Father & Son Road Trip · Memorials, Museums & Battlefields
description: Follow the D-Day and Battle of Normandy story across France with this self-guided field map. Tap a marker on the map, or pick a stop from the list to fly straight to it. Tap the circle next to a name to mark it visited as you go.
howTo: Tap a marker on the map, or pick a stop from the list to fly straight to it. Tap the circle next to a name to mark it visited as you go.

footer.built: Field guide to the Western Front · Built with React & Tailwind

stay.title: Find a cozy stay
stay.hint: Open B&Bs, guesthouses & converted monastery hotels near this spot.

dunkirk.name: Dunkirk (Dunkerque)
dunkirk.hours: Memorial & harbour always open; museum: Tue–Sun
dunkirk.blurb: The beach and harbour from which the British Expeditionary Force was evacuated in May 1940.
dunkirk.context: Operation Dynamo evacuated some 338,000 Allied soldiers from the beach and harbour as the German army closed in, one of the war's most dramatic rescues.
dunkirk.tip: Visit the Dunkirk Memorial and the wartime museum on Route des Bains.

blockhaus-eperlecques.name: Blockhaus d'Éperlecques
blockhaus-eperlecques.blurb: A giant unfinished Nazi bunker built to launch V-2 rockets at London.
blockhaus-eperlecques.context: This huge unfinished concrete bunker was built to launch V-2 rockets at London. It never became operational, but stands as a striking monument to the secret 'V-weapon' campaign.
blockhaus-eperlecques.tip: Giant concrete slab nicknamed 'the Blockhouse' — allow an hour for the bunker trail.

la-coupole.name: La Coupole
la-coupole.blurb: A huge concrete dome originally meant to store V-2 rockets, now a museum.
la-coupole.context: A vast concrete dome designed to store, prepare and launch V-2 rockets. Damaged by Allied bombing before completion, it is now a museum of rocket science and the German occupation.
la-coupole.tip: The planetarium and history centre are worth the visit on a rainy day.

batterie-todt.name: Batterie Todt
batterie-todt.blurb: A German coastal battery near Cap Gris-Nez with a massive armoured turret.
batterie-todt.context: One of Germany's biggest coastal batteries, guarding the Channel with 280 mm guns in the giant Casemate 1 along with a range of smaller casemates.
batterie-todt.tip: Visit the adjacent 1944 museum and climb the dunes for sea views.

fortress-mimoyecques.name: Fortress of Mimoyecques
fortress-mimoyecques.blurb: A secret underground V-3 cannon complex built into the chalk hills.
fortress-mimoyecques.context: A secret underground complex of inclined shafts built to fire V-3 'super-guns' at London. The flat roofs were never finished after heavy bombing.
fortress-mimoyecques.tip: The shaft network is reached by lift — very atmospheric underground.

fort-de-la-creche.name: Fort de la Crèche
fort-de-la-creche.blurb: A restored 19th-century fort at Cap de la Crèche re-used by the Germans in WWII.
fort-de-la-creche.context: A 19th-century fort reoccupied and re-armed by the Germans, who added concrete casemates overlooking the approaches to Boulogne.
fort-de-la-creche.tip: Combine with a walk along the clifftop coastal path.

musee-39-45-ambleteuse.name: Musée 39-45 Ambleteuse
musee-39-45-ambleteuse.blurb: A private collection of WWII military objects and memorials at Ambleteuse.
musee-39-45-ambleteuse.context: A private museum of WWII objects, uniforms and weaponry exhibited in the historic Moulin de la Belle-Croix at Ambleteuse.
musee-39-45-ambleteuse.tip: Compact collection, great for a quick stop between sites.

memorial-caen.name: Mémorial de Caen
memorial-caen.blurb: Caen's vast museum of WWII and the Battle for Normandy.
memorial-caen.context: Caen's major museum tells the story of France from the pre-war years through occupation and the Battle of Normandy to peace — ending in a Memorial for Peace.
memorial-caen.tip: Set aside half a day — the Peace Memorial is one of Europe's finest.

merville-battery.name: Merville Battery
merville-battery.blurb: The fortified German gun battery stormed by British paratroopers before dawn on D-Day.
merville-battery.context: British 6th Airborne paratroopers stormed the battery just after midnight on D-Day to stop its guns firing on Sword Beach.
merville-battery.tip: Live history tours and re-enactments run in summer.

pegasus-bridge.name: Pegasus Bridge
pegasus-bridge.hours: Bridge always open; memorial museum: Daily 10:00–18:00
pegasus-bridge.blurb: The famous bridge over the Caen canal captured by British glider troops in the first minutes of D-Day.
pegasus-bridge.context: Men of the 6th Airborne's glider force captured the bridge over the Caen canal in minutes, the very first action of D-Day.
pegasus-bridge.tip: The old bridge has been moved next to the new memorial museum.

memorial-pegasus.name: Pegasus Memorial
memorial-pegasus.blurb: Museum next to Pegasus Bridge telling the story of the glider assault.
memorial-pegasus.context: The museum at Bénouville tells the story of the 6th Airborne Division, from glider landings to their vital bridgehead over the Orne.
memorial-pegasus.tip: See the preserved Horsa glider and the original Pegasus Bridge.

ouistreham-atlantic-wall.name: Atlantic Wall Museum — Ouistreham
ouistreham-atlantic-wall.blurb: A restored German bunker complex at Sword Beach.
ouistreham-atlantic-wall.context: This restored German anti-aircraft battery at the mouth of the Orne defended the approaches to Ouistreham, at the eastern end of Sword Beach.
ouistreham-atlantic-wall.tip: Climb to the top of the 'Riva-Bella' battery for a wide view of the beach.

sword-beach.name: Sword Beach
sword-beach.blurb: The easternmost D-Day landing beach, stormed by the British 3rd Division.
sword-beach.context: The easternmost landing beach, stormed by the British 3rd Division, which pushed inland toward Caen with the help of the airborne landings behind the lines.
sword-beach.tip: Walk the promenade at Ouistreham and visit the D-Day sculpture.

juno-beach.name: Juno Beach
juno-beach.blurb: The Canadian landing beach, later linked up with Commonwealth forces.
juno-beach.context: The Canadian landing beach, where the 3rd Canadian Division came ashore under heavy fire and advanced deeper inland than any other sector that day.
juno-beach.tip: Lovely wide strand; the centre is busy in high summer.

juno-beach-centre.name: Juno Beach Centre
juno-beach-centre.blurb: Canada's memorial to its role in the Normandy landings.
juno-beach-centre.context: Canada's memorial centre at Courseulles-sur-Mer commemorates the Canadians who landed on Juno and the civilians of Normandy.
juno-beach-centre.tip: Check the guided bunker tour times on arrival.

beny-sur-mer-cemetery.name: Bény-sur-Mer Canadian War Cemetery
beny-sur-mer-cemetery.blurb: Resting place for nearly 2,000 Commonwealth soldiers, many from Juno Beach.
beny-sur-mer-cemetery.context: Nearly 2,000 Commonwealth soldiers lie here, most of them Canadians killed landing on Juno and in the fighting inland.
beny-sur-mer-cemetery.tip: A quiet, moving stop — white crosses in regular rows.

hillman-strongpoint.name: Hillman Strongpoint
hillman-strongpoint.blurb: A large German strongpoint near Colleville-Montgomery captured on D-Day.
hillman-strongpoint.context: A large German command strongpoint near Colleville-Montgomery, a key objective taken on D-Day after heavy close-quarter fighting.
hillman-strongpoint.tip: Free to walk the trenches and bunkers across the fields.

gold-beach.name: Gold Beach
gold-beach.blurb: The central British landing beach, where the Mulberry harbour was built.
gold-beach.context: The British 50th Division landed here and took seven kilometres of beachfront, near where the Phoenix caissons of the Mulberry harbour later came ashore.
gold-beach.tip: Best combined with Arromanches and the Port Winston remains.

arromanches.name: Arromanches-les-Bains
arromanches.hours: Beach always open; D-Day museum: Daily 09:00–19:00
arromanches.blurb: Site of the Mulberry 'Port Winston' artificial harbour.
arromanches.context: Arromanches lay at the heart of 'Port Winston', the Mulberry artificial harbour that let the Allies unload thousands of tons of supplies each day.
arromanches.tip: View the concrete caissons from the beach or the clifftop viewpoint.

arromanches-360.name: Arromanches 360°
arromanches-360.hours: Daily; film shows through the day
arromanches-360.blurb: Circular cinema showing archival film of the D-Day landings.
arromanches-360.context: A panoramic cinema presenting the D-Day landings on nine screens, built next to the remnants of the Mulberry harbour.
arromanches-360.tip: The wide-screen film runs continuously — check show times.

longues-sur-mer-battery.name: Longues-sur-Mer Battery
longues-sur-mer-battery.hours: Site always open; closed Mon off-season
longues-sur-mer-battery.blurb: A German gun battery on a clifftop, its casemates still intact.
longues-sur-mer-battery.context: This German battery of four casemated 150 mm guns sat on the clifftop overlooking Gold Beach; its guns were silenced by shelling the day after D-Day.
longues-sur-mer-battery.tip: Walk from the car park down to the cliff for the best view.

british-normandy-memorial.name: British Normandy Memorial
british-normandy-memorial.hours: Site always open; visitor centre: Apr–Oct
british-normandy-memorial.blurb: Memorial to the British soldiers who died in Normandy in summer 1944.
british-normandy-memorial.context: Ranks of tall columns list over 22,000 names of British service men and women who died in Normandy between D-Day and the end of August 1944.
british-normandy-memorial.tip: The columns list over 20,000 names; very moving at sunset.

normandy-american-cemetery.name: Normandy American Cemetery
normandy-american-cemetery.blurb: The vast American cemetery above Omaha Beach, overlooking the English Channel.
normandy-american-cemetery.context: Some 9,387 American servicemen rest here overlooking Omaha Beach, their white crosses and stars laid in perfect lines across green lawns.
normandy-american-cemetery.tip: Arrive before the guided tours; soften your voice — it is a place of remembrance.

overlord-museum.name: Overlord Museum
overlord-museum.blurb: Museum by Omaha Beach displaying vehicles, uniforms and D-Day objects.
overlord-museum.context: Displaying tanks, vehicles, uniforms and personal objects, this museum retraces Operation Overlord and the Battle of Normandy around Omaha Beach.
overlord-museum.tip: Near the American cemetery, easy to combine with it.

omaha-beach.name: Omaha Beach
omaha-beach.blurb: The 'Bloody Omaha' American landing beach, the hardest-fought on D-Day.
omaha-beach.context: The bloodiest of the landing beaches, where the US 1st and 29th Divisions met fierce German fire from the bluffs before breaking inland.
omaha-beach.tip: Walk from the memorial down onto the sand for quiet reflection.

wn60.name: WN60 Strongpoint
wn60.blurb: One of Omaha Beach's German defensive positions, opposite the American cemetery.
wn60.context: A German strongpoint above the beach whose positions faced the American cemetery headland; its defences were among those the Americans had to silence.
wn60.tip: Look for the remains in the dunes near the beach.

wn62.name: WN62 Strongpoint
wn62.blurb: Famous German emplacement at Omaha that fired on the first landing waves.
wn62.context: From this emplacement German troops fired on the first waves at Omaha; it has become the best-known symbol of the beach's deadly defences.
wn62.tip: Interpretation boards explain the D-Day morning hour by hour.

d-day-omaha-museum.name: D-Day Omaha Museum
d-day-omaha-museum.blurb: A collection of Omaha Beach war relics in Vierville-sur-Mer.
d-day-omaha-museum.context: A private collection in Vierville-sur-Mer of weapons, vehicles and personal items recovered from Omaha Beach.
d-day-omaha-museum.tip: Small private museum with wreckage and personal items.

pointe-du-hoc.name: Pointe du Hoc
pointe-du-hoc.blurb: The dramatic clifftop stormed by US Rangers, still pockmarked with craters.
pointe-du-hoc.context: US Rangers scaled the 30-metre cliff under fire to destroy heavy guns, finding them withdrawn; the headland remains cratered by the bombardment.
pointe-du-hoc.tip: Walk the battle-scarred headland and see the surviving gun casemates.

la-cambe-german-cemetery.name: La Cambe German War Cemetery
la-cambe-german-cemetery.blurb: Germany's largest military cemetery in Normandy, with over 21,000 graves.
la-cambe-german-cemetery.context: More than 21,000 German soldiers are buried here, marked by dark stone crosses in a peaceful grove — a sombre counterpart to the other Normandy cemeteries.
la-cambe-german-cemetery.tip: The contrast with the American cemetery is quietly thought-provoking.

airborne-museum.name: Airborne Museum — Sainte-Mère-Église
airborne-museum.blurb: Museum in Sainte-Mère-Église dedicated to the US airborne landings.
airborne-museum.context: In Sainte-Mère-Église, the museum honours the US 82nd and 101st Airborne, telling of the night drop that preceded the seaborne landings.
airborne-museum.tip: See the C-47 'Douglas' and the story of the famous parachute on the church tower.

sainte-mere-eglise.name: Sainte-Mère-Église
sainte-mere-eglise.hours: Town always open; museum: see Airborne Museum
sainte-mere-eglise.blurb: One of the first towns liberated, parachuted into by US airborne troops.
sainte-mere-eglise.context: One of the first towns liberated in Europe, taken by US paratroopers in the small hours — a parachute still hangs from its church tower.
sainte-mere-eglise.tip: Spot the parachute hanging from the church steeple.

utah-beach.name: Utah Beach
utah-beach.blurb: The westernmost landing beach — the 4th US Division landed here at H-Hour.
utah-beach.context: The westernmost landing beach; the US 4th Division came ashore here and linked up with the airborne troops inland faster than expected.
utah-beach.tip: Long open beach; the monument and dunes are worth the walk.

utah-beach-museum.name: Utah Beach Museum
utah-beach-museum.blurb: Museum at the actual landing site by the water's edge.
utah-beach-museum.context: Located at the actual landing site, the museum occupies a restored control post and retells the Utah landing through film and objects.
utah-beach-museum.tip: Views across the beach from the landing-craft setting are powerful.

azeville-battery.name: Azeville Battery
azeville-battery.blurb: A well-preserved German coastal battery inland from Utah Beach.
azeville-battery.context: A German coastal battery re-used after D-Day; its surviving bunkers and passages now offer guided visits showing how the garrison lived.
azeville-battery.tip: Guided tours explore the dark underground passages.

la-fiere.name: La Fière
la-fiere.blurb: Site of intense fighting over the causeway bridge held by American paratroopers.
la-fiere.context: At the causeway bridge over the Merderet, US paratroopers held off a German counterattack in some of the fiercest fighting of the airborne campaign.
la-fiere.tip: The bridge and the Iron Mike monument mark a key D-Day crossroads.

dead-mans-corner.name: Dead Man's Corner Museum
dead-mans-corner.blurb: Museum at a famous crossroads tenement fought over by airborne troops.
dead-mans-corner.context: At this crossroads near Carentan, named for a paratrooper found there, airborne troops fought intense close-quarters battles in June 1944.
dead-mans-corner.tip: Interesting private collection in the original building.

carentan.name: Carentan
carentan.hours: Town always open; Victory Museum: see below
carentan.blurb: Strategic town captured by the 101st Airborne, key to joining the beachheads.
carentan.context: Captured by the 101st Airborne after days of street fighting, Carentan joined the Utah and Omaha beachheads into a single front.
carentan.tip: Walk the town centre and see the church of Notre-Dame.

normandy-victory-museum.name: Normandy Victory Museum
normandy-victory-museum.blurb: Museum at Carentan covering the full Battle of Normandy.
normandy-victory-museum.context: At Carentan, large dioramas with life-size figures and vehicles retell the whole Battle of Normandy from D-Day to the liberation of Paris.
normandy-victory-museum.tip: Large set-piece dioramas with life-size soldiers and vehicles.

bayeux-battle-of-normandy-museum.name: Bayeux Battle of Normandy Museum
bayeux-battle-of-normandy-museum.blurb: Museum of the British side of the Battle of Normandy.
bayeux-battle-of-normandy-museum.context: This museum examines the war from the British perspective, following Commonwealth forces from D-Day to the crossing of the Seine.
bayeux-battle-of-normandy-museum.tip: Combine with the nearby Bayeux Tapestry if you have time.

bayeux-war-cemetery.name: Bayeux War Cemetery
bayeux-war-cemetery.blurb: The largest Commonwealth cemetery in France, with over 4,000 graves.
bayeux-war-cemetery.context: The largest Commonwealth war cemetery in France holds over 4,000 graves, mostly British soldiers who died in the Battle of Normandy.
bayeux-war-cemetery.tip: Peaceful and impeccably tended; a short walk from the town centre.

saint-lo.name: Saint-Lô
saint-lo.blurb: A key crossroads town, heavily destroyed and fought over in July 1944.
saint-lo.context: The crossroads town of Saint-Lô was fought over street by street in Operation Cobra's opening days and largely reduced to rubble.
saint-lo.tip: See the 'Moon Over Normandy' sculpture in the town centre.

montormel-memorial.name: Montormel Memorial
montormel-memorial.blurb: A memorial at the site of the closing of the Falaise pocket.
montormel-memorial.context: High above the Dives, this memorial marks the closing of the Falaise pocket, where the encircled German army was trapped and destroyed.
montormel-memorial.tip: The diorama explains the encirclement of the German army.

falaise-pocket.name: Falaise Pocket
falaise-pocket.blurb: The battlefield where the German army was encircled and destroyed in August 1944.
falaise-pocket.context: In the pocket between Falaise and Argentan, the German armies were surrounded by the Allies; tens of thousands were killed or captured in the mop-up.
falaise-pocket.tip: Drive the country lanes to grasp the scale of the encirclement.

menin-gate.name: Menin Gate Memorial
menin-gate.hours: Always open; the Last Post sounds nightly at 20:00
menin-gate.blurb: The great memorial to 54,896 missing soldiers of the Ypres Salient, and home of the nightly Last Post.
menin-gate.context: The vast Menin Gate lists the 54,896 Commonwealth soldiers with no known grave who fell in the Ypres Salient. Since 1928, buglers have played the Last Post beneath its arches every single night at 20:00 — the only ceremony of its kind in the world.
menin-gate.tip: Arrive well before 20:00 — the nightly Last Post ceremony draws a large crowd.

in-flanders-fields-museum.name: In Flanders Fields Museum
in-flanders-fields-museum.blurb: Ypres' Cloth Hall is home to an immersive museum of the First World War.
in-flanders-fields-museum.context: Housed in the rebuilt Cloth Hall at the heart of Ypres, the museum tells the story of WWI in the Salient through personal stories, including the Canadian poet John McCrae, who wrote 'In Flanders Fields' at nearby Essex Farm.
in-flanders-fields-museum.tip: The rooftop walkway gives a superb view over the reconstructed medieval town.

essex-farm-cemetery.name: Essex Farm Cemetery & Dressing Station
essex-farm-cemetery.blurb: A battlefield cemetery beside the original aid post where John McCrae wrote his famous poem.
essex-farm-cemetery.context: This cemetery on the Ypres–Brielen road lies next to a preserved underground dressing station. It was here, in May 1915, that Canadian officer John McCrae composed 'In Flanders Fields' after burying a friend.
essex-farm-cemetery.tip: Look for the preserved tunnels and the memorial plaque to McCrae's poem.

hill-60.name: Hill 60
hill-60.blurb: A famous artificial hill shaped by craters and tunnels, the scene of fierce mining and trench fighting.
hill-60.context: Hill 60 was a crucial observation point fought over throughout the war. In April 1915 the Germans launched the first major gas attack of WWI here, and the landscape is still pockmarked by the craters of the great mining war.
hill-60.tip: The walk around the craters, trenches and bunkers is short but striking.

tyne-cot-cemetery.name: Tyne Cot Cemetery
tyne-cot-cemetery.blurb: The largest Commonwealth war cemetery in the world, final resting place of nearly 12,000 soldiers.
tyne-cot-cemetery.context: Tyne Cot crowns the ridge and holds nearly 12,000 graves — the greatest number of Commonwealth burials anywhere. It was built on ground taken by Allied troops at Passchendaele in 1917, and the Memorial to the Missing bears over 34,000 names.
tyne-cot-cemetery.tip: Climb to the top for a vast panorama over the battlefield where the 'Passchendaele' mud was won.

passchendaele-museum.name: Memorial Museum Passchendaele 1917
passchendaele-museum.blurb: An atmospheric museum recreating the dugouts and mud of the 1917 Passchendaele offensive.
passchendaele-museum.context: In Zonnebeke Château, the museum powerfully re-creates the British and German dugouts of the Third Battle of Ypres (Passchendaele), including reconstructed underground shelters and a re-created flooded battlefield.
passchendaele-museum.tip: A reconstructed network of underground dugouts brings trench life vividly to mind.

langemark-cemetery.name: Langemark German Cemetery
langemark-cemetery.blurb: A sombre German war cemetery — a counterpart to the Commonwealth cemeteries nearby.
langemark-cemetery.context: Langemark is one of the few German cemeteries in the Salient, holding around 44,000 dead in dark, flat ranges of graves — a moving contrast to the white stones of the Commonwealth sites. In 1914 the German reserve troops sang here before advancing.
langemark-cemetery.tip: Its dark, sunken graves feel very different from the Allied cemeteries — worth seeing both.

polygon-wood.name: Polygon Wood / Buttes Cemetery
polygon-wood.blurb: A long-contested wood with preserved trenches, bunkers and its own hilltop cemetery.
polygon-wood.context: Polygon Wood was fought over for years; the 'Buttes' on its crest held the British line. Remains of concrete shelters, trenches and shell craters still scar the woods today.
polygon-wood.tip: Find the butte and its cemetery, then follow the short battlefield trail through the trees.

vimy-ridge.name: Vimy Ridge Canadian Memorial
vimy-ridge.blurb: The soaring Canadian memorial on the ridge taken in the Battle of Vimy Ridge in April 1917.
vimy-ridge.context: The towering twin-pylon Canadian National Vimy Memorial crowns the ridge with 20,000 names of the missing. In April 1917 all four Canadian divisions fought together for the first time to capture the ridge, a defining moment for Canada.
vimy-ridge.tip: Book ahead to tour the preserved underground tunnels and trenches of the battlefield.

thiepval-memorial.name: Thiepval Memorial
thiepval-memorial.blurb: The immense memorial to the missing of the Somme, commemorating over 72,000 soldiers.
thiepval-memorial.context: The vast red-brick Thiepval is the largest Commonwealth memorial in the world, bearing more than 72,000 names of soldiers with no known grave from the Somme battles of 1916–1918. It rises above the ridge where the first day of the Somme was fought.
thiepval-memorial.tip: The visitor centre and the view across the former battlefield are both unmissable.

beaumont-hamel.name: Beaumont-Hamel Newfoundland Memorial
beaumont-hamel.blurb: A preserved 1 July 1916 battlefield with trenches and the lone caribou statue in memory of the Newfoundland Regiment.
beaumont-hamel.context: The Beaumont-Hamel site preserves a section of the Somme battlefield as it was on the first day. The Newfoundland Regiment was decimated here in the morning of 1 July 1916; the bronze caribou, the emblem of the regiment, stands over the ground.
beaumont-hamel.tip: The park's preserved trenches and mine craters let you trace the attack lines on foot.

lochnagar-crater.name: Lochnagar Crater
lochnagar-crater.blurb: The largest crater left by a mine explosion anywhere, on the first day of the Somme.
lochnagar-crater.context: At 07:28 on 1 July 1916, a 27-tonne mine detonated here, blasting one of the largest craters ever made by a single explosion and signalling the start of the Battle of the Somme. The crater is now privately preserved as a memorial.
lochnagar-crater.tip: Walk right down into the crater to grasp its astonishing scale.

notre-dame-de-lorette.name: Notre-Dame-de-Lorette
notre-dame-de-lorette.blurb: France's largest military cemetery and the memorial to the battles of Artois.
notre-dame-de-lorette.context: The hill of Notre-Dame-de-Lorette holds more than 20,000 French graves and the remains of another 20,000 in ossuaries — France's largest military cemetery. It commemorates the bitter 1915 Artois offensives around Arras.
notre-dame-de-lorette.tip: Climb the ring of light at the top — a modern memorial on the hill.

compiegne-armistice.name: Compiègne Armistice Clearing
compiegne-armistice.blurb: The clearing in the forest where the Armistice ending WWI was signed on 11 November 1918.
compiegne-armistice.context: In a clearing in the Forest of Compiègne, on 11 November 1918, the Armistice was signed in a railway carriage, ending WWI. The carriage was destroyed in 1940 after the second, harsher armistice was signed in the same place — a replica now stands inside the memorial museum.
compiegne-armistice.tip: The evocative memorial museum is built around a faithful reproduction of the 1918 railway carriage.

douaumont-ossuary.name: Douaumont Ossuary & Verdun
douaumont-ossuary.blurb: The moving ossuary holding the remains of soldiers from the 1916 Battle of Verdun.
douaumont-ossuary.context: The Douaumont Ossuary holds the remains of over 130,000 unidentified soldiers from the 300-day Battle of Verdun, the longest battle of WWI. Nearby, Fort Douaumont still bears the scars of the fighting that consumed the village below.
douaumont-ossuary.tip: Pair the ossuary with Fort Douaumont and walk the preserved battlefield remains nearby.
